thread:
maya: heads-up — seeing a cluster-wide uptick in ECC correctables on ashburn pool-gpu-12, started ~09:02 UTC, rate ramping.
opsbot: ALERT gpu_ecc_correctable_rate high on pool-gpu-12 (card ids: 3,7,11) — 3xx/min over last 8m :rotating_light:
dina: can you paste the query you used? want to correlate with Xid spikes and host power cycles
maya: querying prometheus now, basic metric I used:
```
sum(increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[10m])) by (card,host)
```
maya: card-3 = 220 in last 10m, card-7 = 190, card-11 = 15 — 3 looks noisy, 11 is small blip
chris: interesting — card-3 and 7 are on the same PCIe switch, any host-level reboots in the same window?
sam: checked host events, host-gpu-12-3 had an ACPI / NMI last night around 02:00 but nothing recent
luis: also saw thermal excursions on that rack yesterday during a datacenter HVAC probe, could be related
dina: agree we should avoid an immediate hard drain. propose: soft-evac (migrate new workloads off, keep running existing tokens) for cards that cross 200 correctables / 10m AND have repeat bursts in 3 consecutive 10m windows.
maya: +1. add hysteresis: require <50/10m sustained for 30m to clear soft-evac. avoid flip-flopping.
chris: for cards that cross 1k/10m or start showing Xid non-zero > 5/min, we should trigger an escalated hard drain and replace workflow.
sam: note capacity impact — pool-gpu-12 is 85% utilized. soft-evac will increase tail latency for batch jobs. we should schedule canary drains during low traffic window if possible.
luis: can we suppress auto-drain for reserved customer workloads? some tenants explicitly disallow preemptive drains.
dina: yes, add tag `no-auto-drain` and treat those cards as manual-only. also send an ops page to the owner.
opsbot: suggested auto-drain policy draft:
```
- soft-evac: conditions: any card with sum(increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[10m])) >= 200 && repeat>=3
  action: set host.eviction_mode = "soft", route new allocs away, alert infra oncall
- hard-drain: conditions: increase(gpu_ecc_uncorrectable_total[5m]) > 5 || xid_errors > 10/min
  action: drain + replace, ticket to hw-ops
- suppression: if host.tags contains "no-auto-drain" -> escalate to manual
- hysteresis: clear soft-evac only after 30m of <50/10m
```
maya: can we add correlation check with `dmesg` PCIe errors too before hard drain? some correctables come from noisy lanes but aren't imminent failures
chris: yes, add a pre-check: `pci_errors > 0` OR `dmesg|grep -i pcie` contains "link error" -> escalate quicker
sam: cost tradeoff: replacing cards too aggressively increases spare consumption and RMA costs. prefer soft-evac + thermal/workload mitigation first.
luis: operational note: during last spike we saw power-cycling the PSU on that node temporarily reduce correctables. maybe power rail stability plays a role.
dina: action items: (1) roll out soft-evac policy to ashburn region with 24h dry-run (no hard-drain), (2) add telemetry for PCIe link errors into the ECC alert context, (3) mark 2 cards as `no-auto-drain` while we consult owners.
maya: I'll open a dashboard and add per-card sparkline to the alert. also attach the last 72h of `gpu_ecc_correctable_total` to the incident for postmortem.
opsbot: created alert draft: https://alerts.internal/redwood/alerts/2345 (dry-run mode)
chris: +1 to dry-run. also add a small runbook blurb for oncall: quick checks -> `promql`, `ssh host`, `dmesg`, check PSU event log.
maya: oncall runbook snippet:
```
1) run: sum(increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[10m])) by (card,host)
2) ssh host -> sudo dmesg | grep -i pcie
3) if xid_errors > 10/min -> file hw-ops ticket
4) if soft-evac conditions met -> set host.eviction_mode=soft
```
sam: thanks. will coordinate scheduling dry-run deploy around 03:00 UTC tomorrow to minimize perf impact.
luis: tagging owners for cards 3 & 7: @infra-team @hw-ops
maya: ok closing thread, we'll reconvene after 24h dry-run. :white_check_mark:
